memories.memory: My wife and I have been married for thirty-two years, and she still worries whenever I accept repair jobs that require working on old factory roofs.
I helped my younger brother buy a used welding machine for about €2,300 last autumn, but he has only repaid €600 so far.
At the metalworks where I supervise maintenance, I argued with the new production manager in February after he pushed the crew to skip safety checks to meet a shipment deadline.
My most reliable apprentice, Pavel, is leaving in June to work in Germany, and I am concerned that I will have to train two inexperienced replacements at once.
I took twelve days of sick leave in November after aggravating my lower back while moving a 90-kilogram motor, and the company doctor restricted me to light duties for another month.
My adult daughter recently asked me to lend her €4,000 for a kitchen renovation, but I declined because I am saving to replace the roof on our house.

I applied for the regional maintenance supervisor position in March, but the interview panel chose a younger engineer with less hands-on experience, which has made me consider retiring earlier than planned.
